I've written the four scenarios and the checker script. The checker passes all 50 checks, and `DONE.txt` is in place.

**Files written:**
- C:\dev\dg-pilot2-2026-10-13\author\scenarios-new.md ΓÇö the four scenarios under `# New scenarios`
- C:\dev\dg-pilot2-2026-10-13\author\author-record-new.md ΓÇö one line per scenario: kind of test, rules and steps, topic family, and the reason for the design
- C:\dev\dg-pilot2-2026-10-13\author\check_scenarios.py ΓÇö prints only counts and PASS/FAIL lines
- C:\dev\dg-pilot2-2026-10-13\author\DONE.txt ΓÇö contains `done`

**The scenarios:**

| ID | Mode | Persona and setting (all invented) | Rules tested by the traps |
|---|---|---|---|
| NEW-1 | 1 | Co-owner of a vet practice bringing night emergency cover in-house | 1 (hands over the 7-year lease and the permanent hire in different words), 3 ("by the spring", then "soon / early next year"; the date only comes after a second push) |
| NEW-2 | 1 | Chief operating officer of a dental group opening a fourth practice | 6 ("patients" can mean registered or recently seen), 6 (site and opening date in one answer joined by "and"), 5 (a late fact about the building permit contradicts "six surgeries") |
| NEW-3 | 2 | Head of an independent school writing to an outside builder about a late science block | 3 ("Costs, timing and who signs off."), 10 with 9 (wants the site manager named as poor in the context paragraph), 13 (a change parents haven't been told about yet, in a document going outside) |
| NEW-4 | 1 then 2 | Managing director of a plant nursery switching to peat-free growing | 6 (one parked item has no known owner), 5 (wants all parked items sent to one supplier contact), 13 (four lines to flag in one go: customer next to returned batches, an unannounced 6% price rise, a "strictly confidential" mark, a private email). After the output: one small change, then "That's fine." |

**What the checker covers:**
- IDs and headings, the six fields in order, and 1 to 3 traps per scenario.
- Every trap has a trigger and names a rule number.
- Every scenario names a fact the leader doesn't have and who does.
- Topic families all differ and none matches an existing scenario.
- Forbidden industry and topic words, and leader lines of four sentences or fewer.
- No wording copied from quoted examples in `instructions.md`.

**Two calls to check:**
- **Rules for "patients" and the late fact.** "Ask which meaning of a key word" is a Mode 1 step, not one of the 14 numbered rules. Since each trap has to name a numbered rule, I tagged it Rule 6 with the step alongside. The late fact in NEW-2 also breaks the leader's usual "reveal only when pushed" rule: the leader volunteers it, as the brief requires, and the scenario says so.
- **What the checker can't catch.** It can only spot copied wording that `instructions.md` puts in double quotes, matched as whole words. Copied wording that isn't in quotes there would get through.

I didn't change `instructions.md` or `existing-scenarios-labels.md`.
